app.title: Morphological Annotation Workbench for Interlinear Glossed Text
app.summary: A person picks a corpus and steps through its utterances one at a time. They can jump straight to the next one that is not yet fully confirmed. Each utterance is shown as interlinear glossed text: surface tokens, morpheme breakdowns and glosses, with every token coloured by whether its analysis is confirmed, suggested or missing. The person highlights a stretch of the utterance or clicks a span. They then rerun the finite-state analyzer on it or add a manual analysis, can ask a language model to propose a reading for every span, and mark one interpretation per span as gold. Along the way they can link the utterance to a linguistic claim as supporting or contradicting evidence, follow gold coverage and gold-versus-candidate agreement in the sidebar, download the glossed utterance as text or LaTeX, and save the corpus.

task.text: Settle on the correct morphological analysis for every span of every utterance in a corpus, choosing among parser-proposed and model-suggested readings, so the corpus becomes fully glossed.

data.text: A corpus of utterances, each with a surface form and a free translation. Every utterance carries candidate morphological analyses over its token spans, each with several interpretations (morpheme breakdown and gloss) that hold gold or candidate labels, along with tags, notes and links to claims.
data.item: an utterance with its token spans and their alternative morphological interpretations

stage.text: glossing a parsed corpus utterance by utterance, after automatic analysis and before claims are drawn from it

mechanism.text: A navigator moves through utterances, and the interlinear display, the highlightable surface text and the span pills are linked. Selecting a stretch in any of them opens that span's analysis panel, where the person stars a gold interpretation or adds a manual one, while LLM suggestions, reanalysis previews and claim linking open as toggled panels below an action bar.

field.text: morphological glossing of interlinear text with a finite-state analyzer, in linguistics

workflow.name: choose the right reading for each segment of every item from machine-proposed options

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: Prev/next buttons, an utterance number box and a 'Next incomplete' button (arrow keys, H/L and N) move through the selected corpus, with a header showing position, status and a gold/analyzed progress bar.
The utterance card shows the surface line, the interlinear morpheme and gloss rows coloured by gold, candidate or unanalyzed status, and the free translation and notes.

steps.step: select a stretch and label it with a category
steps.here: Highlighting text or clicking an IGT cell or span pill selects an analysis or a gap. 🔄 Analyze reruns the FST on the selection for a commit-or-discard preview, and ➕ Manual creates a hand-made analysis, offering to delete the analyses it overlaps.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The 🤖 Suggest panel asks an LLM, at a chosen reasoning effort, to pick one interpretation per span using the translation. Single-option spans are picked automatically, and the results are shown with justifications before 'Apply as candidates'.

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: In the span panel each interpretation card has a gold star and a candidate toggle plus a note. The person confirms one reading per span as gold, which records who confirmed it and when.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: The sidebar Metrics show utterances that are fully gold or candidate, analyses with no label, analyses the LLM declined, and the gold-versus-candidate agreement rate, flagging disagreements for reconciliation.
Per-utterance IGT downloads as plain text or LaTeX (gb4e), utterances link to claims as evidence, and the corpus is saved to SQLite with a backup or synced to Drive.

distinctive: Candidate analyses come from a finite-state morphological analyzer. Spans with no analysis show as red gap pills, which the person can fill by reanalyzing or entering a manual analysis.
Labels come in two tiers: an LLM-applied 'candidate' and a human-confirmed 'gold', and the agreement rate between them is tracked across the corpus.
Each utterance can be attached as supporting, contradicting or neutral evidence to a linguistic claim, with a required note.
Editing is locked behind a password, and every gold or candidate label records the annotator and a timestamp.
Glossed examples export in LaTeX gb4e format, ready to paste into a paper.

parts.title: Corpus selector and utterance navigator
parts.summary: Picks the corpus and moves through its utterances, including a jump to the next one not fully confirmed, with a status line and progress bar.

parts.title: Utterance with interlinear gloss
parts.summary: Shows the utterance's surface text for highlighting, plus clickable interlinear rows of tokens, morphemes and glosses coloured by annotation status.

parts.title: Action bar
parts.summary: Buttons to edit the utterance, show tags, link a claim, probe in the Analyzer, ask for LLM suggestions, rerun the analyzer or add a manual analysis on the selection, and download the IGT as text or LaTeX.

parts.title: Span analysis panel
parts.summary: Lists every span as a pill and opens the selected span's interpretation cards, where the person stars one as gold, toggles a candidate, adds notes or interpretations, or deletes the analysis.

parts.title: Link to claim
